summary: @greenlake/auth postinstall beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package declares `postinstall: node beacon.cjs` and additionally fires the same beacon from `index.js` on require(). The beacon POSTs a JSON payload containing `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and the Node version to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`, which is unrelated to any `@greenlake` publisher infrastructure. The package otherwise ships no functional code: `index.js` self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and exports a Proxy whose `get` trap returns a no-op for every property access. The shape — a `@scope/<name>` no-op shim whose only behavior is identifying the installing host to an attacker-controlled IP on `npm install` — matches the dependency-confusion probe pattern, where a public package is published under an internal scope name to map which corporate installers resolve to the public registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
